answer_raw:
The top cities vary depending on whether you prioritize stability and infrastructure or economic strength and human capital.

**Copenhagen** is the world's most liveable city according to the EIU Global Liveability Index as of July 2026, earning a score of **98 out of le 100** [6][8]. The EIU index assesses 173 cities across five categories: stability, healthcare, culture and environment, education, and infrastructure [1].

The **Oxford Economics 2026 Global Cities Index** offers a different perspective, ranking 1,000 cities based on economic strength, human capital, environment, and quality of life [2][3][5]. In this ranking, **New York** takes the No. 1 spot overall, though it is noted that US cities as a group struggle specifically in the quality of life category, where only one US city made the top 20 cut [3]. **Canberra** also performs well in quality of life metrics like life expectancy and recreation, even though it ranks 45th in the overall index [2].

**Monocle's** own quality of life survey, released in July 2026, places **Paris** at the top [7]. This ranking focuses on factors like safety, connectivity, governance, and green space, noting that North American cities have struggled due to crime, inequality, and housing issues [4].

| Ranking Body | Top City (as of source date) | Primary Focus |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **EIU** [6][8] | **Copenhagen** (July 2026) | Stability, healthcare, education, and infrastructure |
| **Oxford Economics** [3] | **New York** (Oct 2026) | Economics, human capital, and environment |
| **Monocle** [7] | **Paris** (July 2026) | Connectivity, governance, and green space |
